title: Probability Distribution Function (PDF) for a Discrete Random Variable

slides.title: A random variable
slides.body: A random variable assigns a numerical value to each outcome of an experiment.
slides.question: For two coin tosses, how could X count the heads?

slides.title: Variable or realization?

slides.body: A model assigns P(X = 2) = 0.4. A single session downloads 3 files.

title: Mean or Expected Value and Standard Deviation

slides.title: Expected value
slides.body: Expected value is the probability-weighted mean of a random variable.
slides.question: What is the expected number of downloads in this synthetic model?

slides.title: The weighted mean formula
slides.body: Each possible value is weighted by its probability.
slides.question: Why should a value with probability 0.4 receive more weight than one with probability 0.1?

slides.title: Not an unweighted average
slides.body: Synthetic model: X = 0, 1, 2, 3 with probabilities 0.1, 0.3, 0.4, 0.2.
slides.question: Why is (0 + 1 + 2 + 3)/4 not the expected value?

slides.title: A mean between integers
slides.body: Synthetic model: X = 0 with probability 0.7 and X = 1 with probability 0.3.
slides.question: Can the expected value be 0.3 even though X never equals 0.3?

slides.title: Interpret the mean
slides.body: A synthetic download-count model has expected value 1.7 files per session.

slides.body: An independent repeated experiment has expected value 1.7 downloads per session.

slides.title: Expected total
slides.body: A synthetic model has expected value 1.7 downloads per session.

slides.body: Variance is the probability-weighted mean squared distance from μ.

slides.title: Same mean, different spread
slides.body: Synthetic model A: X is always 1. Model B: X = 0 or 2, each with probability 0.5.
slides.question: Which model has larger standard deviation?

slides.title: Model versus sample
slides.body: One statistic summarizes observed session counts; another summarizes their proposed probability distribution.
slides.question: Which uses s, and which uses σ?

slides.body: Synthetic server selection: A is chosen with probability 0.4 and takes 2 seconds; B with probability 0.6 takes 5 seconds.
